subject: bakery
title: Model Question Paper 1
meta: Time: 2 hours · Maximum marks: 40 · Modelled on the April 2026 NIOS paper (code 256)
instructions: All questions are compulsory and carry marks as indicated against each question.
Question 1: fifteen fill-in-the-blanks (1 mark each). Question 2: fifteen True/False statements (1 mark each). Question 3: four questions of 2½ marks each.
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

sections.title: Fill in the blanks and write the correct answers.

questions.q: A proving chamber, oven and table are all ________ equipment.
Milk contains about ________ per cent water.
Macaroons are made of almond, sugar and ________.
Macaroons have a ________ texture.
Victoria cake is made by the ________ method.
In the creaming method the fat should be soft but not ________.
________ icing is used for both icing cakes and making cake decorations.
________ is a clay like paste made out of ground almonds.
________ juice is added to strengthen the gluten in flaky and puff pastry.
Flour with good quality gluten is required for ________ pastry.
Too dark reddish brown colour of crust in bread is due to too much ________.
The ideal temperature for fermentation of bread dough should be ________.
Danish pastry is served in ________.
questions.answer: Breakfast (as a coffee or breakfast bread).

questions.q: The process of transferring entries from journal to ledger is called ________.
Net profit is gross profit minus ________ cost.

sections.title: State whether the following statements are True or False.

questions.q: A fresh egg sinks in water.
The temperature of an electric oven cannot be controlled.
questions.answer: False. An electric oven has a thermostat which makes temperature regulation easier.

questions.q: Warm water is used for binding the ingredients of short crust dough.
questions.answer: False. Ice cold water is used.

questions.q: 'Knock back' is a process during biscuit preparation.
questions.answer: False. Knocking back is a process in bread making.

questions.q: The base of a Swiss roll is a fatless sponge.
Victoria is a type of bread.
'Marzipan' is chocolate based.
questions.answer: False. It is made from almonds and sugar.

questions.q: Butter icing can be stored at room temperature for a fortnight.
questions.answer: True. The room should be well ventilated.

questions.q: The amount of fat used in flaky paste is more than that in puff paste.
questions.answer: False. Puff paste has more fat (1:1) than flaky paste (3/4:1).

questions.q: Warm or tap water should be used for mixing pastry.
The liquid used in breads is always water.
questions.answer: False. It may be milk or water.

questions.q: Brown bread is made by using brown colour.
questions.answer: False. It is made with white flour and whole meal flour in equal quantities.

questions.q: Danish pastry is made from a yeast puff dough.
Property accounts are recorded under real account.
Primary entry is the first step in accounting.
questions.answer: True. The transaction is first recorded in the journal.

sections.title: Answer the following questions (five points each).

questions.q: Describe the preparation of biscuits by the creaming method.
questions.answer: (i) Cream fat and sugar until the mixture is light and fluffy, since air bubbles are forced into the batter. (ii) Add egg and beat again. (iii) Sieve flour and baking powder and mix in gently, a little at a time, without kneading. (iv) Roll, cut with biscuit cutters and place on a greased tray. (v) Bake at about 160 C for 10-12 minutes and cool on a cooling rack.

questions.q: Mention one reason each for the following faults in cake: (i) white spots on cake surface (ii) cake baked with peeled top (iii) cake with flat top (iv) cracks on surface of cake (v) discoloured crumb.
questions.answer: (i) White spots: too much sugar, batter standing too long or very large sugar grains. (ii) Peeled top: insufficient mixing or too much heat from the top. (iii) Flat top: oven too cool or incorrect balance between fat and egg. (iv) Cracks on the surface: too hot an oven. (v) Discoloured crumb: too much bottom heat or too much baking powder.

questions.q: Name the basic 5 pastes made in bakery.
questions.answer: (i) Short crust paste. (ii) Flaky paste. (iii) Puff paste. (iv) Choux paste. (v) Danish paste.

questions.q: Find the selling price needed to get a gross profit of 65% on selling price if the cost of raw material of a cake is Rs. 18. Also find the net profit when a confectionery has a gross profit of Rs. 1,000, labour cost Rs. 450 and overhead cost Rs. 425.
questions.answer: (i) Material cost = 100% - 65% = 35% of the selling price. (ii) 35% = Rs. 18, so 1% = 18/35 and 100% = 18/35 x 100 = Rs. 51.43. (iii) Net profit = gross profit - overhead - labour. (iv) = 1,000 - 425 - 450 = Rs. 125.
